title: Ops Toolkit: graft adapters for runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Marceline Cho
description: Introduce a small, composable set of "graft" adapters in the Ops Toolkit that let teams mount existing runbooks and admin utilities as first-class task primitives. Each graft will wrap a runbook fragment, expose a typed input schema, telemetry hooks, and safety gates (dry-run / canary) so Support and SRE can orchestrate automated remediation without bespoke scripting.
background: We have dozens of ad-hoc runbook snippets and one-off admin scripts in repos and docs. On-call engineers frequently copy/paste and maintain slightly different variants across teams. This increases toil and reduces trust in automation. The graft approach standardizes small adapters that "bridge" runbook artifacts into the runlet/task runtime so they behave like other task primitives (idempotent, typed, auditing-ready).
goals: Provide a minimal graft adapter API (Python/Go) that wraps a runbook fragment and registers it with the admin task registry
Ship 3 production grafts for common incident types (cache invalidation, config rollback, model restart)
Ensure every graft emits structured telemetry and has a dry-run mode
Enable RBAC gating and audit log hooks for executed grafts
acceptance_criteria: Graft adapter library published to ops-toolkit with tests and README
Three grafts live behind a feature flag in staging and exercised in chaos-run replay
Console shows per-graft telemetry (invocations, success/failure, duration) in the operator dashboard
Playbook authors can declare typed inputs (schema) that validate prior to execution
All graft executions produce an audit entry and are reversible via documented rollback steps
implementation_plan: Design graft adapter API (lib + CLI) and propose schema for inputs/outputs
Prototype Python graft for cache invalidation flow, include dry-run toggles
Add telemetry hooks to the runtime and map to console metrics
Create RBAC integration: map graft IDs to policy entries, enforce in runtime
Staging rollout behind feature flag; run tabletop and chaos scenarios with SRE
Iterate on UX based on Support feedback and move to GA after 2-week bake
risks: Accidental destructive automation if typed inputs are not validated — mitigated by strict schema and dry-run default
Too many bespoke grafts leading back to fragmentation — mitigate via graft review cadence and registry governance
Telemetry cardinality growth if we log every intermediate step — mitigate by sampling and summary metrics
metrics: Time to remediate for graft-covered incidents (target: -30% median)
Number of manual steps avoided (target: 3 common runbooks automated)
Graft invocation success rate (>99% after GA)
Audit log volume per graft (kept under quota)
rollout_notes: Feature-flag first in staging for two weeks. Invite SRE and Support to an early access channel. After stability signals and telemetry validation, flip to org-wide opt-in. Document governance for adding grafts to the registry.
